pathway.title: CVR ENERGY INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings are at a cyclical peak and one quarter carries most of it. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 317 million in FY2024 and USD 393 million in FY2025, then USD 828 million in the first nine months of 2026, and Petroleum Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 127 million to USD 621 million as the NYMEX 2-1-1 crack spread averaged USD 55.16 against USD 25.62. The issuer takes the crack spread as given, so the mechanism is an external margin that can reverse within a quarter, and creditors should treat last-twelve-months coverage of 6.96x as a peak reading. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_d897437dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2 and 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C2

Leverage is low today but roughly doubles on earlier-year earnings. Total debt of USD 1,781 million is 1.94x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, 4.53x the FY2025 figure and 5.62x the FY2024 figure, and annual fixed coupons of about USD 120.71 million are covered 7.61x by the last twelve months but only 3.26x at the FY2025 level. The leverage reduction came from earnings, not debt repayment, because total debt moved from USD 1,765 million to USD 1,781 million over the nine months, so earnings at the FY2025 level would put leverage close to the 4.49x of year-end 2025. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C5

Liquidity and maturities give a long runway on the existing structure. Cash of USD 1,278 million (cash pro forma for the declared dividend, the CVR Partners distribution and the acquisition is not established) and undrawn credit facilities of USD 575 million make USD 1,853 million, 2.53 times the USD 733 million of notes that fall due in 2028, and the largest credit facility matures in 2031. The runway is narrower than it looks because USD 158 million of the cash sits in the consolidated nitrogen partnership and the company has agreed to hold at least USD 500 million of unrestricted cash until the acquisition closes or the agreement ends. Net debt of USD 503 million is USD 513 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, and the pro forma figure after the acquisition and the CVR Partners distribution is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C6

Free cash flow is real but volatile and partly timing. House free cash flow after capital and turnaround spending was USD 872 million in nine months of 2026 against negative USD 238 million in FY2025 and USD 172 million in FY2024, so conversion of Adjusted EBITDA ranged from 105.31% to negative 60.56% to 54.26%. The 2026 figure benefits from USD 132 million of income tax that was accrued but not yet paid and from only USD 2 million of turnaround spending, with the next major turnaround scheduled for 2027, so durable conversion is lower than the nine-month figure suggests. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 27 and 61; calculation C7

The Renewable Fuel Standard is a second earnings driver and a cash contingency. Waivers removed obligations of about USD 488 million in August 2025 and about USD 253 million in August 2026 and appear as non-cash gains in reported EBITDA, while the accrued obligation is USD 230 million; if challenges succeed, reinstating the USD 253 million would equal 27.53% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA in cash. This is why Adjusted EBITDA, not reported EBITDA, is the better coverage base, and why a ruling date, not a quarter's results, can reset the cash position. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25 and 58; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8

The acquisition would change the credit more than any operating trend. The cash consideration of about USD 4,200 million is 4.57x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and 2.36 times existing total debt, and the named backstops include a secured bridge of up to USD 2,500 million that alone equals 2.72x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. The sources give no sources and uses table, no target earnings and no bridge draw, so pro forma debt and leverage are not established, and secured bridge debt would rank ahead of the USD 1,183 million of CVR Energy unsecured notes on pledged assets. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12 and 32; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9

Control and structure add leakage that consolidated figures hide. One holder owns about 71% of the stock, the controlled-company exemptions are in use, and the nitrogen partnership paid USD 67 million of its USD 110 million of nine-month distributions to public unitholders and USD 3 million to the controlling holder, so CVR Energy received about 19.51% of nitrogen EBITDA. Creditors of the CVR Energy notes therefore hold a claim on a group whose consolidated cash and EBITDA overstate what reaches them, and the documented sponsor record, a dividend suspended in October 2024 and no priming or drop-down disclosed, is mixed rather than adverse. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11 and 62

runs.text: The strongest support is liquidity and the maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,853 million exceeds total debt, all credit lines are undrawn and nothing falls due before 2028, so debt service in the next two years depends on earnings only at the margin. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C6

A second strength is a low-cost regional crude position. The gathering system supplied about 67% of Coffeyville and 94% of Wynnewood crude demand in FY2025, and the two refineries ran at 100.1% of capacity in 2026, so margin capture rests on owned logistics, which the annual report describes as a transportation cost advantage over crude sourced elsewhere. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_d897437dex991.htm.jsonl, page 9

A third strength is a second earnings stream with separate funding. The nitrogen partnership earned USD 205 million of EBITDA in nine months against USD 191 million, funds itself through its own secured notes and credit facility, and diversifies away from refining margins, although its cash is only partly available to CVR Energy. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57 and 62

A fourth strength is a refinancing record that cleared the 2027 to 2029 maturities. The February 2026 issue of USD 1,000 million of notes and the credit facility extension moved the nearest note maturity to 2028 and the facility to 2031, which reduces refinancing risk before the acquisition. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main weakness is earnings that depend on external margins and rulings. Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is 2.34x the FY2025 figure, 63.33% of it from one quarter, and waivers that can be challenged lifted reported results, so the leverage ratios can reverse faster than debt can be repaid. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C13

A second weakness is the pending acquisition, which adds debt, execution and integration risk while funding terms are unknown. Secured bridge debt of up to USD 2,500 million would sit ahead of the unsecured notes, and no pro forma leverage is stated. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation C9

A third weakness is concentrated control with weak visibility into limits. One holder controls the issuer, relies on the controlled-company exemptions, and the indentures, credit agreements and board independence are not in the sources, so protection against leakage cannot be tested. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

A fourth weakness is unquantified legal, environmental and operating exposure. An ammonia release, class claims in Kansas, a guaranty dispute and an EPA settlement project are open, and the filings do not size them, so they limit confidence in the liquidity runway. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26 and 34

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The largest transaction in the sources is the agreement of November 2, 2026 to acquire two refineries, pipeline interests and marketing and logistics assets from affiliates of Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4,200 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments and regulatory approvals. The company intends to fund it from cash on hand, credit-facility borrowings, permanent senior secured financing, the equity investments and a registered equity offering, backed by a bridge of up to USD 2,500 million, USD 550 million of extra credit-facility commitments, a USD 800 million convertible preferred placement and up to USD 500 million of equity from the controlling holder. It expects to close before the end of 2026, and it must hold at least USD 500 million of unrestricted cash until then. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12 and 31–32

The only new debt issued in the period is the USD 1,000 million of senior notes of February 12, 2026, made up of USD 600 million of the 2031 notes and USD 400 million of the 2034 notes, with net proceeds of USD 993 million. The proceeds repaid the term loan, redeemed all the 2029 notes and redeemed USD 217 million of the 2028 notes, and the credit facility was extended to February 2031 with commitments of USD 550 million. The 2031 and 2034 notes are guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by domestic subsidiaries other than CVR Partners. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 151–152; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 annual report, three 2026 quarterly reports and three results releases cover the statements, debt, liquidity and segment results, and the latest report was signed two days before the as-of date. The pending Marathon refinery purchase, priced at about USD 4.2 billion, is described only in the third quarter report and release, so a pro forma debt figure is not established in these sources.

fields.value: - Executed financing and acquisition documents are not in the source set. The indentures for the 2028, 2031 and 2034 notes and for the 2028 nitrogen fertilizer notes, the two asset-based credit agreements, the Marathon purchase agreement, the debt commitment letter and the equity subscription agreements are described in the filings but not supplied, and the run settings declare no legal documents. Covenant terms are known only as the filings summarise them, so Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control and Recovery & fulcrum cannot be assessed. This is a material gap for those modules and a limitation, not a block, for the requested route.

fields.value: Debt barely moved while earnings changed the ratios. Total debt was USD 1,919 million at the end of 2024, USD 1,765 million at the end of 2025 and USD 1,781 million at September 30, 2026, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose from USD 394 million in FY2024 and USD 591 million in FY2025 to USD 964 million. Total debt to EBITDA therefore fell from 4.87x to 2.99x and then 1.85x, and net debt to EBITDA from 2.37x to 2.12x and then 0.52x. The mechanism is operating, not balance-sheet: the nine-month 2026 refining result carried the figure, so creditors hold a ratio that depends on refining margins they do not control.

fields.value: Reported EBITDA is flattered by non-cash refining-obligation gains, so the adjusted measure is the better coverage base. Favorable changes in the Renewable Fuel Standard obligation sit in reported EBITDA and are removed from Adjusted EBITDA: USD 262 million in FY2025 and USD 190 million in the first nine months of 2026, which includes the USD 253 million liability removed by the August 2026 waiver. The 2026 adjustment also adds back USD 278 million of unrealized derivative losses and removes USD 173 million of favorable inventory valuation. EBITDA to cash interest was 4.16x reported against 2.77x adjusted in FY2025, and is 7.30x reported against 6.96x adjusted over the last twelve months. A creditor who sized FY2025 cover on the reported figure would have overstated it by 1.39x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The last twelve months hold one record quarter, and the rest were far weaker. Implied fourth-quarter 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was USD 91 million (the annual USD 393 million less nine months of USD 302 million), the first half of 2026 added USD 246 million, and Q3 2026 alone was USD 582 million, which the company calls the best quarter in its history, so the last twelve months of USD 919 million hold 63.33% from one quarter. Had Q3 2026 matched the USD 180 million of Q3 2025, last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA would be USD 517 million and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA 3.44x, an illustration rather than a forecast. The low leverage and 6.96x adjusted cover are therefore as fragile as one quarter's refining margins, and the fourth-quarter outlook the company gives covers operations and capital spending only, not earnings.

fields.value: Cash generation was real but part of it is timing. Operating cash flow was USD 1,026 million over nine months of 2026 against USD 144 million a year earlier, and capital expenditure plus turnaround spending fell to USD 154 million from USD 326 million as the next turnaround is not until 2027. Of the operating cash flow, USD 132 million is accrued income tax not yet paid and USD 278 million is a non-cash derivative loss added back, so the tax payable is a cash call still to come. Cash rose by USD 767 million to USD 1,278 million even after USD 20 million of dividends and USD 70 million of distributions to the nitrogen unitholders, and the company-defined free cash flow was USD 878 million.

fields.value: Liquidity is ample and nothing is drawn, but not all of the cash is freely available. Cash of USD 1,278 million plus USD 530 million available under the CVR Energy credit facility (USD 550 million of available capacity less USD 20 million of letters of credit) and USD 45 million under the CVR Partners facility gives USD 1,853 million, up from USD 807 million at the end of 2025. Cash was USD 512 million at March 31 and USD 737 million at June 30 on total debt of USD 1,784 million and USD 1,783 million, so the build came in the third quarter. Of the cash, USD 158 million sits in CVR Partners, which is consolidated but is a separate borrower with its own secured notes and credit facility, and the company has agreed to hold at least USD 500 million of unrestricted cash until the acquisition closes or the agreement terminates. The CVR Energy facility matures in February 2031 and the CVR Partners facility in September 2028, so no committed line expires within twelve months.

fields.value: The 2026 refinancing cleared the near-term wall and left a 2028 cluster. In February 2026 the company issued USD 1,000 million of new senior notes and used them to repay the USD 157 million term loan, redeem all USD 600 million of the 2029 notes and redeem USD 217 million of the 2028 notes. Contractual principal is now USD 1,733 million, of which USD 733 million falls due in 2028: USD 183 million of unsecured 2028 notes at CVR Energy and USD 550 million of secured 2028 notes at CVR Partners. The fixed coupons on these notes come to about USD 120.71 million a year, and the carrying value of USD 1,781 million exceeds principal by USD 48 million because finance leases of USD 61 million sit inside debt and USD 13 million of issuance costs are deducted.

fields.value: The consolidated figures combine two separate creditor groups. CVR Partners carries USD 569 million of debt net of current portion, including its secured 2028 notes of USD 550 million, and USD 158 million of cash, and the filings do not describe any CVR Energy guarantee of it, while the three CVR Energy notes of USD 1,183 million are expressly not guaranteed by CVR Partners. Noncontrolling holders took USD 70 million of distributions in nine months, cash that leaves the consolidated total without reaching CVR Energy's own creditors. Holders of the CVR Energy notes therefore rely on the petroleum business and on distributions that the partnership shares with outside unitholders, and the 0.52x consolidated net leverage nets nitrogen cash against the debt of both groups, so it cannot be read as the position of CVR Energy's own noteholders.

The accrued renewable fuel obligation was USD 230 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 72 million at the end of 2025, derivative liabilities were USD 160 million, and accrued income taxes USD 132 million, all inside other current liabilities and none in debt. At the end of 2025 the company also reported purchase commitments of USD 165 million and transportation agreements of USD 995 million, and operating lease liabilities of USD 64 million; these are outside the debt figure and are cash calls that compete with debt service. Lawsuits over an ammonia release, environmental claims in Kansas and a guaranty dispute are not quantified, so they are a limit on certainty rather than a number.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending acquisition is the main event after the balance sheet date and is not in any figure above. On November 2, 2026 the company agreed to buy two refineries and related assets from Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4,200 million in cash, backed by a commitment for a 364-day secured bridge of up to USD 2,500 million, USD 550 million of extra credit-facility commitments, a USD 800 million convertible preferred placement and up to USD 500 million of equity from the controlling holder. The sources do not say how much of the bridge will be drawn or when the deal closes, so pro forma debt and leverage are not established; a termination fee of 2% to 6% of the base price applies if the agreement ends in specified ways. A declared dividend of USD 10 million is payable on November 23, 2026.

fields.value: The view that leverage is a peak reading has real counter-evidence. Net debt of USD 503 million is only 0.52x reported EBITDA and 0.55x Adjusted EBITDA, liquidity of USD 1,853 million exceeds total debt by USD 72 million, no note or loan matures before 2028, the company states it complied with all covenants at September 30, 2026, and the third quarter alone produced free cash flow of USD 593 million. The quarter that drops out of the window next is the weak fourth quarter of 2025, so if refining margins stay near the third-quarter level the last twelve months would rise again and the favorable reading would hold. The view weakens further if the acquisition closes with the bridge drawn in full, because USD 2,500 million of new secured debt would rank ahead of the unsecured notes on any pledged assets against USD 919 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, or 2.72x.

Icahn Enterprises and its affiliates owned about 71% of the common stock at September 30, 2026 against about 70% at the end of 2025, the company relies on all three controlled-company exemptions from the independent-board requirements, and a sale of the controlling stake could oblige the issuers to offer to repurchase the notes at 101% of principal and could be an event of default under both credit facilities. The controlling holder therefore influences board composition, dividends, financing and acquisitions, and creditors can only test that influence through indentures and credit agreements that are not in the source set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refining margin and regulation, not scale, drive creditor risk. Refining supplied 93.40% of sales in the nine months of 2026 and 89.58% in FY2025, and the two refineries ran at 100.1% of crude capacity against 75.6% a year earlier, when the 2025 Coffeyville turnaround took capacity out. The refining margin was USD 19.28 per barrel against USD 15.93, and the NYMEX 2-1-1 crack spread averaged USD 55.16 against USD 25.62, so the improvement owes much to price, which the issuer does not control, as well as to the volume recovery. The nitrogen business is only 6.60% of sales but produced 22.45% of nine-month EBITDA, so a small revenue line carries a large part of earnings and sits in a separate creditor group.

fields.value: The Renewable Fuel Standard turns a regulatory ruling into earnings and into a cash claim. The Wynnewood subsidiary is an obligated party, and the EPA waived its obligation by about USD 488 million in August 2025 and by about USD 253 million in August 2026, while the accrued obligation was USD 230 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 72 million at the end of 2025. Waiver gains are non-cash and can be challenged: challenges are pending in the federal appeals court and the EPA proposed in October 2026 to spread the 2025 exempted volumes over 2026 and 2027 or add them to 2027, so a successful challenge would reinstate an obligation and turn an earnings gain into a cash outflow on RIN purchases, which the company already accrues in full for 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor payout behaviour is moderate against cash generation and responded to weaker earnings. Total dividends were USD 453 million in 2023 and USD 151 million in 2024, of which the controlling holder received USD 311 million and USD 100 million, and house free cash flow after capital and turnaround spending was USD 686 million and USD 172 million. The board suspended the dividend in October 2024 as margins fell, none was paid in 2025, and payments resumed in 2026 at USD 10 million in each of the second and third quarters, USD 20 million over nine months against house free cash flow of USD 872 million. That record supports a mixed rather than extractive reading, but it is also a record of discretion: nothing supplied limits the next distribution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition shifts the creditor question from past payouts to how the next USD 4,200 million is funded. On November 2, 2026 the issuer agreed to buy two Marathon Petroleum refineries and related assets for about USD 4,200 million in cash. The named backstops are a senior secured 364-day bridge of up to USD 2,500 million, a USD 800 million convertible preferred placement with a commercial counterparty and up to USD 500 million of equity from the controlling holder, which total USD 3,800 million, so about USD 400 million plus fees would come from cash on hand, credit-facility borrowings or an equity offering. The sources give no sources and uses table, no pro forma EBITDA and no bridge draw, and the controlling holder's commitment ends if the company completes an equity offering of at least USD 500 million, so sponsor support is committed rather than funded. The company has agreed to hold at least USD 500 million of unrestricted cash until closing or termination.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management changed in mid-2026 while the finance chair is interim. A separation agreement with the former chief executive and an employment agreement with the former chief financial officer, now chief executive, are both dated June 18, 2026, and the third quarter report is signed by an interim chief financial officer who is also the vice president of financial planning and investor relations. The auditor issued an unqualified opinion with no critical audit matters, but a thin finance bench during a USD 4,200 million transaction raises execution and reporting risk that creditors cannot test, because the proxy statement with board independence and compensation is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVR Partners is consolidated but only partly reachable by CVR Energy creditors. The issuer owns about 37% of the common units and all of the general partner, public unitholders hold about 60% and the controlling holder about 3%, and the partnership's own executives are CVR Energy employees under a services agreement that can be ended on 90 days' notice, which creates a stated conflict of interest. Of USD 110 million distributed in nine months of 2026, CVR Energy received USD 40 million, public unitholders USD 67 million and the controlling holder USD 3 million, so CVR Energy received about 19.51% of the nitrogen EBITDA of USD 205 million. Consolidated cash and EBITDA therefore overstate what is available to holders of the CVR Energy notes, which the CVR Partners subsidiaries do not guarantee.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Unquantified legal and environmental matters sit beside the debt. An ammonia release at the Coffeyville fertilizer facility in October 2025 has produced consolidated suits in Texas and a further suit in August 2026, class claims over environmental conditions in Kansas are in discovery, a guaranty dispute over alleged historical well contamination is stayed during mediation, and a flare gas recovery project of about USD 53 million is being installed under the 2023 EPA settlement. The company describes these matters as early-stage and possibly material, so the exposure is a limit on certainty and a possible call on liquidity rather than a number.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a mixed reading is the combination of control, discretion and a large pending deal. The controlling holder received USD 311 million of dividends in 2023, relies on the controlled-company exemptions, is considering further strategic transactions that include options for CVR Partners, and is providing up to USD 500 million of equity into the acquisition at the same price per share as an outside investor. The evidence for a more favourable reading is that the dividend was suspended when earnings fell, no uptier, drop-down, priming or creditor-adverse amendment appears in the sources, and the 2026 refinancing replaced a secured term loan and the 2029 notes with unsecured notes. The view would turn adverse if the bridge is drawn in full and dividends continue, if the equity commitment is replaced by a public offering that is smaller than the need, or if the indentures show wide restricted-payment capacity; it would improve if the sponsor funds equity before closing and the final structure keeps unsecured creditors' position intact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by concentrated control and a pending secured-debt-funded acquisition, because they let one holder shape distributions and financing, which implies that creditor position after closing depends on documents not supplied. Countervailing evidence is the suspension of dividends when earnings fell, a refinancing that cut secured debt, and committed sponsor equity. Further analysis requires the credit agreements, indentures and the closing financing. Governance and sponsor assessment completed with limitations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The largest transaction in the sources is the agreement of November 2, 2026 to acquire two refineries, pipeline interests and marketing and logistics assets from affiliates of Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4,200 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments and regulatory approvals. The company intends to fund it from cash on hand, credit-facility borrowings, permanent senior secured financing, the equity investments and a registered equity offering, backed by a bridge of up to USD 2,500 million, USD 550 million of extra credit-facility commitments, a USD 800 million convertible preferred placement and up to USD 500 million of equity from the controlling holder. It expects to close before the end of 2026, and it must hold at least USD 500 million of unrestricted cash until then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt issued in the period is the USD 1,000 million of senior notes of February 12, 2026, made up of USD 600 million of the 2031 notes and USD 400 million of the 2034 notes, with net proceeds of USD 993 million. The proceeds repaid the term loan, redeemed all the 2029 notes and redeemed USD 217 million of the 2028 notes, and the credit facility was extended to February 2031 with commitments of USD 550 million. The 2031 and 2034 notes are guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by domestic subsidiaries other than CVR Partners.

fields.value: CVR ENERGY INC (issuer id cvi), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the issuer's fundamental credit profile from the seven supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance module outputs. It does not assess covenants, recovery, relative value or position size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVR Energy's liquidity exceeds its total debt today, but its earnings are cyclical and driven by commodity prices and regulation, so creditors are covered now and exposed to a sharp reversal and to how the pending USD 4,200 million acquisition is financed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million, of which Q3 2026 supplied 63.33%, compares with USD 393 million in FY2025, so total debt of USD 1,781 million is 1.94x Adjusted EBITDA today and would be 4.53x at the FY2025 level. Liquidity is USD 1,853 million and no note matures before 2028. Net debt of USD 503 million is USD 513 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03; net debt pro forma for the acquisition and the CVR Partners distribution is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are at a cyclical peak and one quarter carries most of it. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 317 million in FY2024 and USD 393 million in FY2025, then USD 828 million in the first nine months of 2026, and Petroleum Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 127 million to USD 621 million as the NYMEX 2-1-1 crack spread averaged USD 55.16 against USD 25.62. The issuer takes the crack spread as given, so the mechanism is an external margin that can reverse within a quarter, and creditors should treat last-twelve-months coverage of 6.96x as a peak reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is low today but roughly doubles on earlier-year earnings. Total debt of USD 1,781 million is 1.94x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, 4.53x the FY2025 figure and 5.62x the FY2024 figure, and annual fixed coupons of about USD 120.71 million are covered 7.61x by the last twelve months but only 3.26x at the FY2025 level. The leverage reduction came from earnings, not debt repayment, because total debt moved from USD 1,765 million to USD 1,781 million over the nine months, so earnings at the FY2025 level would put leverage close to the 4.49x of year-end 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities give a long runway on the existing structure. Cash of USD 1,278 million (cash pro forma for the declared dividend, the CVR Partners distribution and the acquisition is not established) and undrawn credit facilities of USD 575 million make USD 1,853 million, 2.53 times the USD 733 million of notes that fall due in 2028, and the largest credit facility matures in 2031. The runway is narrower than it looks because USD 158 million of the cash sits in the consolidated nitrogen partnership and the company has agreed to hold at least USD 500 million of unrestricted cash until the acquisition closes or the agreement ends. Net debt of USD 503 million is USD 513 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, and the pro forma figure after the acquisition and the CVR Partners distribution is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is real but volatile and partly timing. House free cash flow after capital and turnaround spending was USD 872 million in nine months of 2026 against negative USD 238 million in FY2025 and USD 172 million in FY2024, so conversion of Adjusted EBITDA ranged from 105.31% to negative 60.56% to 54.26%. The 2026 figure benefits from USD 132 million of income tax that was accrued but not yet paid and from only USD 2 million of turnaround spending, with the next major turnaround scheduled for 2027, so durable conversion is lower than the nine-month figure suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Renewable Fuel Standard is a second earnings driver and a cash contingency. Waivers removed obligations of about USD 488 million in August 2025 and about USD 253 million in August 2026 and appear as non-cash gains in reported EBITDA, while the accrued obligation is USD 230 million; if challenges succeed, reinstating the USD 253 million would equal 27.53% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA in cash. This is why Adjusted EBITDA, not reported EBITDA, is the better coverage base, and why a ruling date, not a quarter's results, can reset the cash position.

fields.value: The acquisition would change the credit more than any operating trend. The cash consideration of about USD 4,200 million is 4.57x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and 2.36 times existing total debt, and the named backstops include a secured bridge of up to USD 2,500 million that alone equals 2.72x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. The sources give no sources and uses table, no target earnings and no bridge draw, so pro forma debt and leverage are not established, and secured bridge debt would rank ahead of the USD 1,183 million of CVR Energy unsecured notes on pledged assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control and structure add leakage that consolidated figures hide. One holder owns about 71% of the stock, the controlled-company exemptions are in use, and the nitrogen partnership paid USD 67 million of its USD 110 million of nine-month distributions to public unitholders and USD 3 million to the controlling holder, so CVR Energy received about 19.51% of nitrogen EBITDA. Creditors of the CVR Energy notes therefore hold a claim on a group whose consolidated cash and EBITDA overstate what reaches them, and the documented sponsor record, a dividend suspended in October 2024 and no priming or drop-down disclosed, is mixed rather than adverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the peak-earnings view is balance-sheet strength that does not depend on the cycle. Total debt is USD 72 million below liquidity, no note matures before 2028, the credit facilities are undrawn, the company states compliance with all covenants, and Q3 free cash flow on the issuer's own definition was USD 593 million, so even a sharp earnings fall leaves several years of runway on the existing structure. The Wynnewood subsidiary has also been relieved by waivers in two successive Augusts, and the refineries ran at 100.1% of crude capacity against 75.6%, which suggests operations, not only price, improved. The view would soften if fourth-quarter results hold near the third-quarter level, because the weak fourth quarter of 2025 drops out of the last twelve months, and if the acquisition closes with more equity than debt. It would harden if the bridge is drawn in full, if the waivers are reversed, or if the closing financing leaves unrestricted cash below the USD 500 million undertaking after the tax and dividend calls already identified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is liquidity and the maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,853 million exceeds total debt, all credit lines are undrawn and nothing falls due before 2028, so debt service in the next two years depends on earnings only at the margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second strength is a low-cost regional crude position. The gathering system supplied about 67% of Coffeyville and 94% of Wynnewood crude demand in FY2025, and the two refineries ran at 100.1% of capacity in 2026, so margin capture rests on owned logistics, which the annual report describes as a transportation cost advantage over crude sourced elsewhere.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third strength is a second earnings stream with separate funding. The nitrogen partnership earned USD 205 million of EBITDA in nine months against USD 191 million, funds itself through its own secured notes and credit facility, and diversifies away from refining margins, although its cash is only partly available to CVR Energy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fourth strength is a refinancing record that cleared the 2027 to 2029 maturities. The February 2026 issue of USD 1,000 million of notes and the credit facility extension moved the nearest note maturity to 2028 and the facility to 2031, which reduces refinancing risk before the acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weakness is earnings that depend on external margins and rulings. Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is 2.34x the FY2025 figure, 63.33% of it from one quarter, and waivers that can be challenged lifted reported results, so the leverage ratios can reverse faster than debt can be repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second weakness is the pending acquisition, which adds debt, execution and integration risk while funding terms are unknown. Secured bridge debt of up to USD 2,500 million would sit ahead of the unsecured notes, and no pro forma leverage is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third weakness is concentrated control with weak visibility into limits. One holder controls the issuer, relies on the controlled-company exemptions, and the indentures, credit agreements and board independence are not in the sources, so protection against leakage cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fourth weakness is unquantified legal, environmental and operating exposure. An ammonia release, class claims in Kansas, a guaranty dispute and an EPA settlement project are open, and the filings do not size them, so they limit confidence in the liquidity runway.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVR Energy is a holding company whose cash flow comes from two mid-continent refineries, a controlling interest in a nitrogen fertilizer partnership and, until December 2025, a renewable diesel unit. Refining supplied 93.40% of nine-month 2026 sales and nitrogen 6.60%; the renewables business, which had an EBITDA loss of USD 22 million in FY2025, ended when the unit reverted to hydrocarbon processing. Bulk refined products are sold to retailers, railroads, farm cooperatives and other refiners at spot prices based on a regional differential, and nitrogen products are sold under fixed-price contracts of less than one year, so revenue visibility is limited to a quarter or two and debt service depends on liquidity rather than contracted revenue. The business is seasonal: refining earnings are lower in the first and fourth quarters, and nitrogen sales are higher in the first half.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 21–22, 26 and 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Icahn Enterprises and its affiliates own about 71% of the common stock, the issuer is a controlled company relying on the exemptions from independent board requirements, and a sale of the controlling stake could trigger a repurchase offer at 101% of principal and a default under both credit facilities. The issuer owns about 37% of the common units and all of the general partner of CVR Partners, which is consolidated, has its own secured notes and credit facility, and is excluded from the guarantees of the CVR Energy notes, while no CVR Energy guarantee of its notes is described. The implication is a two-tier creditor structure in which structural priority at the nitrogen assets sits with CVR Partners creditors, and leverage tolerance, dividends and acquisitions are set by one holder; the sponsor record is mixed, with dividends suspended in October 2024 and equity of up to USD 500 million committed to the acquisition, and the legal limits on leakage are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is price and volume driven with little pass-through protection. Nine-month 2026 net sales rose 49.48% to USD 8,000 million on higher gasoline and distillate prices and higher throughput volumes after the 2025 turnaround, and the refining margin was USD 19.28 per barrel against USD 15.93, yet the issuer is a price taker on both crude and products. The largest petroleum customer was 12% of petroleum sales and the top two nitrogen customers 28% of nitrogen sales in FY2025, so concentration is moderate, and nitrogen prices followed global commodity markets, with UAN at USD 348 per ton against USD 307. Revenue is therefore cyclical, commodity-linked and not contracted, which is why creditors should lean on liquidity and maturities rather than revenue visibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22 and 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9 and 46; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_d897437dex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Most cost is crude and feedstock, so margins depend on the spread, not on cost control. Cost of materials was 79.98% of nine-month 2026 net sales and direct operating expenses 7.16%, direct operating cost per barrel fell to USD 6.06 from USD 6.62 while utilization rose, and commodity derivative losses of USD 516 million in the nine months show that hedging transfers risk between periods rather than removing it. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.35% in nine months of 2026 against 5.49% in FY2025, so margins can be defended in a strong spread year but not under a spread squeeze, because fixed operating cost and a turnaround cycle remain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9 and 19; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_d897437dex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is moderate but lumpy and the cash conversion shown for 2026 is flattered. Capital spending of USD 147 million in nine months of 2026 was 66.67% maintenance, the 2026 estimate is USD 220 million to USD 240 million, and growth projects include an alkylation unit of about USD 155 million due in late 2027 and a flare gas system of about USD 53 million. Turnaround cash was USD 197 million in FY2025 and USD 2 million in nine months of 2026, and the next major turnaround falls in 2027, so house free cash flow of USD 872 million should not be annualised. Cash interest of USD 132 million over the last twelve months, finance leases and the unpaid income tax are the other main calls on that cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 34 and 60–61; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is price-based: the issuer competes with several regional refineries and with product moved in by pipeline, and nitrogen is a global commodity market with larger producers, so margins are set by the market and cannot be defended by the issuer. The sources do not discuss new entry; as an Analyst Judgement the capital intensity of refining limits it, which supports the issuer's regional position. Substitution has already hit the renewable diesel unit, which the issuer reverted for poor economics, and the regulatory credit regime, not product substitution, is the live threat. Buyer power is moderate: the largest refining customer is 12% of sales, though nitrogen contracts are short. Supplier power is contained by the owned gathering system, but the remaining crude depends on pipelines subject to proration, and pet coke for the Coffeyville fertilizer plant came 36% from the adjacent refinery in 2025, so an outage at one site affects the other.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and the commodity economy are primary credit drivers; social and technology factors are not. The Renewable Fuel Standard, waiver decisions and pending appeals move earnings and cash, an EPA settlement requires a flare gas project, and agricultural and refining prices set both segments' margins, so these two categories are included. Other categories do not appear to be primary credit drivers based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: liquidity and a 2028 maturity profile, regional crude supply, a second earnings stream in nitrogen, and a refinancing record, each of which supports debt service on the existing structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses: earnings concentrated in one quarter, dependence on external margins and rulings, controlled-company governance with limits not visible, and unquantified legal and environmental exposure, each of which raises the chance that leverage reverses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities: closing the acquisition with a large equity component, a restart of growth capital funded from cash flow, and the nitrogen capacity expansion of about 5%, each of which would improve scale or earnings if executed without adding unsecured claims behind secured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats: reversal of the RFS waivers, a sharp fall in crack spreads, a bridge drawn in full on closing, and a change of control, each of which would hit liquidity or leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 25 and 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are strong spreads and full utilization, with fourth-quarter guidance of 95% to 100% crude utilization, and the headwinds are seasonally weaker refining quarters, the 2027 Wynnewood turnaround, the unpaid tax and the closing of the acquisition. Over three to five years the main supports are the extended credit facility and the 2028 notes being the next maturity, while the 2028 cluster of USD 733 million, a larger post-acquisition debt stack and a possible reinstatement of waived obligations are the main pressures. Each tailwind supports free cash flow and deleveraging only if margins hold, and each headwind pressures liquidity or refinancing confidence, so the outlook is balanced on the existing group and negative on a combined group whose financing is not stated.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_d897437dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34 and 61; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with the crack spread reverting from USD 55.16 toward the USD 25.62 of nine months of 2025. Refining margin falls first, and Petroleum Adjusted EBITDA returns toward the USD 199 million of FY2025, taking consolidated Adjusted EBITDA back to the USD 393 million of FY2025. Leverage on existing debt becomes 4.53x and fixed-coupon cover 3.26x, and house free cash flow turns negative as it did in FY2025 if a turnaround resumes. The calls already identified, USD 132 million of accrued income tax, a USD 10 million dividend and, if waivers were reversed, USD 253 million, total USD 395 million, or 21.32% of liquidity, so the existing structure would not reach liquidity distress inside the next year; management levers are a dividend suspension as in October 2024, deferred growth capital and the undrawn facilities. The first real break is market access, not cash: with the acquisition closed and a secured bridge drawn, USD 2,500 million of secured debt would rank ahead of USD 1,183 million of unsecured notes at a time when earnings had fallen, and the observable triggers are the crack spread, Petroleum Adjusted EBITDA, the bridge draw and any waiver reversal. Primary downside path: a crack-spread reversal coinciding with a debt-funded closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, CVR ENERGY INC presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, regional crude supply and a second earnings stream, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in a peak quarter, a regulatory contingency and a pending debt-funded acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate on the existing group and not fully assessable for the combined group, because free cash flow swung between negative USD 238 million and USD 872 million across periods. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on crack spreads, the closing financing and the outcome of the waiver challenges, and the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established. The primary downside path is a margin reversal that meets a debt-funded closing. Further analysis would require the indentures and credit agreements, the closing financing, target earnings and ratings. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: refining-margin reversal combined with the acquisition's secured financing.
